topic: Messianic Pronoun Capitalization Policy in Greek OT
scope_refs: Capitalized currently (9 anchors + spans): Ps 2:7-9, Ps 44:7-8, Ps 109:1-7, Isa 7:14-16, Isa 9:5-6, Isa 11:2-5, Isa 11:10, Mic 5:1,3,5, Zech 9:9-10, Zech 12:10

Lowercased currently: Gen 3:15, Gen 41:38 (πνεῦμα θεοῦ), Gen 49:10, Gen 49:24 (ὁ κατισχύσας Ἰσραήλ), Job 27:3 (πνεῦμα θεῖον), Ps 86:5, Isa 42:1-4, Isa 49:1-6, Isa 52:13-53:12, Isa 61:1, Lam 4:20, Dan 7:14
summary: OT Modern English applies reverential capitals to unambiguous royal/Messianic passages (Ps 2, 44, 109; Isa 7, 9, 11; Mic 5; Zech 9, 12) while leaving the Servant Songs (Isa 42, 49, 52-53, 61), Gen 3:15, Gen 49:10, Dan 7:14, and Lam 4:20 lowercase. Because capitalization of pronouns in Messianic prophecies is an interpretive/doctrinal choice absent from Greek uncials, a qualified human editor must ratify the exact boundary list.
options: A: Keep current split (capitalize traditional direct-title Messianic texts; keep Servant Songs & Gen/Dan lowercase).
B: Extend reverential capitalization to Servant Songs (Isa 42, 49, 52-53, 61) and Dan 7:14.
C: Reserve reverential capitalization strictly for direct references to God/Lord (κύριος/θεός) in OT and lowercase all Messianic-figure pronouns.
pass2_finding: All 14 OT Messianic/Spirit anchor notes verified and applied with zero verse-text edits. Underlying capitalization boundary remains open for qualified human editor ratification.
pass2_recommendation: Option A (retain current split with the 14 newly applied Rule 4 notes) or explicitly ratify Option B/C across the full span.

topic: πίστις Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ (Objective vs. Subjective Genitive) Policy
summary: Current Modern-English-NT renders Pauline πίστις [Ἰησοῦ] Χριστοῦ passages objectively ('faith in Jesus Christ') with alternate-reading footnotes (Pass 1 proposes adding missing footnotes at Rom 3:26, Gal 2:20, and expanding Jas 2:1), while Jas 2:1 retains the ambiguous English genitive ('the faith of'). Because objective ('faith in Christ') vs. subjective ('faithfulness of Christ') carries major theological weight in Pauline soteriology, human editorial sign-off is required.
options: A: Retain objective 'faith in' in Pauline loci with explicit alternate-reading footnotes at every locus (including newly proposed Rom 3:26, Gal 2:20) and keep 'the faith of' + note at Jas 2:1.
B: Render 'faith of Jesus Christ' where English allows natural ambiguity, with footnotes explaining both objective and subjective senses.
C: Adopt subjective 'faithfulness of Jesus Christ' in Pauline loci with footnotes giving objective 'faith in'.
pass2_finding: Verified Rom 3:22 and Gal 2:16 already carry alternate-reading footnotes; applied neutral Rule 4 footnotes at Rom 3:26, Gal 2:20, and Jas 2:1 with zero verse-text edits. Objective vs. subjective genitive rendering in Pauline loci remains queued for human editorial sign-off.
pass2_recommendation: Option A (retain objective "faith in" with uniform Rule 4 footnotes on every Pauline locus, plus "the faith of" + note at Jas 2:1).

B: Render anarthrous πνεῦμα lowercase ('a spirit' / 'wind') across Ezekiel and Isa 32:15, 63:14, with footnotes noting 'the Spirit'.
C: Capitalize 'the Spirit' uniformly across Ezekiel and Isa 32:15, 63:14 with footnotes noting 'a spirit / wind'.

topic: OT Proper-Name Transliteration Policy (Traditional English/Hebrew vs. Greek LXX Forms)
summary: Modern-English-OT uses conventional English biblical names where the Greek represents the same underlying biblical figure (e.g., Joshua son of Nun for Ἰησοῦς υἱὸς Ναυή in all 29 occurrences), while transliterating uniquely Greek LXX forms when they diverge structurally (e.g., Sareira, Balaennor, Chermel, and Stage 1 Swete/B forms in 1 Chronicles 5-7: Boe, Joanas, Somea, Hama, Asaba, Eaal, Theie, Maasai, Echa, Bokai, Aliareia, Amioueid, Eleimasai). docs/OT-NAME-DECISIONS.json remains provisional; human editorial policy is needed on how far to preserve Codex B/Swete orthography vs. traditional English forms in 1 Chronicles and Joshua.
options: A: Keep conventional English names for well-known biblical figures (Joshua, Nun, etc.) and transliterate Swete/B forms in Stage 1 1 Chronicles 5-7 where Codex B materially diverges from Sixtine/MT.
B: Systematically preserve Greek LXX proper-name forms throughout OT (e.g., Nave for Ναυή, Esaias, etc.).
C: Assimilate 1 Chronicles 5-7 Swete/B proper-name corruptions to conventional English forms with footnotes citing the Codex B Greek forms.
pass2_finding: Pass 2 independently caught an intra-sentence contradiction in Pass 1's isolated 1 Chr 5:35 proposal (GRC-P1-042, rejected): SGCT reads Ἰωανάς in BOTH 5:35 and 5:36, and 5:36 renders it "Johanan." Pass 2 applied mandatory wrong-verse replacement at 1 Chr 7:26 and factual "Seraiah" -> "Zerahiah" at 6:36 plus corrected notes at 6:19 and 6:36, while holding 5:31 (Boe/Bukki), 5:35-36 (Joanas/Johanan), 6:15, 6:19 (Eaal/Theie), 6:25, 6:28, 6:36 (Bokai/Bukki), and 6:37 (Aliareia/Amariah) for unified human editorial policy.
pass2_recommendation: Adopt a unified rule for Codex Vaticanus/Swete genealogical forms in 1 Chr 5-7 (either Option C conventional English + footnotes citing Codex B forms, or Option A applied consistently to paired verses such as 5:35-36 and 5:31/6:36).

topic: Daniel Βαλτασάρ ('Baltasar' for both Belteshazzar and Belshazzar)
summary: Greek Theodotion Daniel uses the single name form Βαλτασάρ for both Daniel's Babylonian court name (Hebrew Belteshazzar) and the Babylonian king of chapter 5 (Hebrew Belshazzar). Current Modern-English-OT preserves 'Baltasar' for both (with clarifying notes) to stay faithful to the Greek source; Claude marked this as a reversible human editorial decision.
options: A: Retain 'Baltasar' for both figures with clear explanatory notes at 1:7 and 5:1 (faithful to Greek Βαλτασάρ).
B: Distinguish 'Belteshazzar' (Daniel's court name) and 'Belshazzar' (King of Babylon) in English while noting that Greek uses Βαλτασάρ for both.
pass2_finding: Confirmed Theodotion Daniel uses Βαλτασάρ for both figures and current ME retains "Baltasar" consistently with clarifying notes; queued for human editorial preference.
pass2_recommendation: Option A (retain "Baltasar" for own-source Greek fidelity with notes at 1:7 and 5:1).

topic: Isaiah 44:5 Bare Dative After Compound ἐπιγράφω ('inscribe on his hand' vs. 'write with his hand')
summary: Adopted Greek reads ἐπιγράψει χειρὶ αὐτοῦ Τοῦ θεοῦ εἰμι. Claude's prior pass changed 'write on his hand' to 'write with his hand' assuming a bare dative must be instrumental, whereas compound ἐπιγράφω ('inscribe upon') regularly takes a locative dative of the surface inscribed. Pass 1 proposes 'inscribe on his hand' with a Rule 4 note giving both readings; human editor to confirm.
options: A: Adopt 'inscribe on his hand' with Rule 4 note citing the instrumental alternative ('write with his hand').
B: Retain 'write with his hand' with Rule 4 note citing the locative surface alternative ('inscribe on his hand').
pass2_finding: Verified Isa 44:5 ἐπιγράψει χειρὶ αὐτοῦ genuinely admits both instrumental ("write with his hand") and locative surface ("inscribe on his hand") senses. Retained current verse text and applied neutral Rule 4 footnote (GRC-P1-118 modified_approved).
pass2_recommendation: Option A ("inscribe on his hand" fits compound ἐπιγράφω naturally) or Option B (retain current text with newly applied Rule 4 note).

topic: Daniel 5:22 Punctuation of οὐ πάντα ταῦτα ἔγνως (Rhetorical Question vs. Statement)
summary: The Studio CT TSV prints an editorial raised dot (·) after οὐ πάντα ταῦτα ἔγνως·, which Claude's prior pass rendered as a declarative denial ('you did not know all these things.'). Because ancient uncials lacked question marks and a denial contradicts Daniel's indictment of Baltasar's willful arrogance in 5:18-23 (and Greek οὐ introduces a rhetorical question expecting 'yes'), Pass 1 proposes restoring 'did you not know all these things?' with a factual note on the CT raised dot.
options: A: Restore rhetorical question 'did you not know all these things?' with a note documenting the CT raised dot.
B: Retain declarative 'you did not know all these things.' following the CT TSV punctuation strictly, with a note explaining the rhetorical-question reading.
pass2_finding: Verified Dan 5:22 SGCT apparatus: Swete prints raised dot (·) whereas both Sixtine/Brenton and Orthodox LXX print question mark (;). Retained current declarative text and upgraded Rule 4 footnote (GRC-P1-145 modified_approved) so both readings are transparently documented.
pass2_recommendation: Option A strongly recommended ("did you not know all these things?" matches Greek interrogative οὐ and Daniel's indictment in 5:18-23 as well as Sixtine/Brenton and Orthodox LXX).

topic: Micah 3:8 Dual Grammatical Attachment of κρίματος καὶ δυναστείας & Anarthrous πνεύματι
summary: Adopted Greek reads ἐὰν μὴ ἐγὼ ἐμπλήσω ἰσχὺν ἐν πνεύματι Κυρίου καὶ κρίματος καὶ δυναστείας. Current English ('by the Spirit of the Lord and of justice and might') awkwardly attaches coordinate genitives to capitalized 'Spirit'. Pass 1 proposes 'by the Spirit of the Lord, and with justice and might,' with a Rule 4 note documenting both syntactic attachments (genitives of filling with ἐμπλήσω vs. coordinated under anarthrous πνεύματι).
options: A: Adopt 'by the Spirit of the Lord, and with justice and might,' plus Rule 4 note on the alternative attachment.
B: Render 'by a spirit of the Lord and of justice and might' (lowercase anarthrous πνεύματι) plus Rule 4 note.
pass2_finding: Verified Mic 3:8 ἐμπλήσω ἰσχὺν ἐν πνεύματι Κυρίου καὶ κρίματος καὶ δυναστείας exhibits genuine syntactic ambiguity. Retained current verse text and applied neutral Rule 4 footnote (GRC-P1-147 modified_approved).
pass2_recommendation: Option A ("by the Spirit of the Lord, and with justice and might,") or Option B (lowercase "a spirit") with the newly applied Rule 4 note.
